articles.title: Pro-Kremlin Russian military blogger Mikhail Zvinchuk arrested in Montenegro
articles.body:
A leading pro-Kremlin Russian military blogger with reported ties to Russia’s intelligence services has been arrested in Montenegro, after warnings of attempts to destabilise the Balkan country, officials have said.
Mikhail Zvinchuk, the founder of the influential Rybar war blog, was detained on Friday alongside his wife and three other Russians by police and security agents in the Adriatic resort town of Risan, on suspicion of spreading Russian influence, local media reported.
Montenegro’s prime minister, Milojko Spajić, confirmed Zvinchuk’s detention in a post on X, saying it followed warnings that the country would face attempts at destabilisation and hybrid warfare.
The Russian Telegram news channel Baza said officers detained Zvinchuk at the luxury Mövenpick hotel in Risan. It said the group was taken to Podgorica, Montenegro’s capital, for questioning and their phones and passports were confiscated.
Founded in 2018 by Zvinchuk, a former press officer at Russia’s defence ministry, Rybar is one of the most popular Russian military blogs covering the war in Ukraine, with more than 1.5 million subscribers on Telegram. It forms part of a sprawling online media ecosystem that promotes Vladimir Putin’s invasion of Ukraine.
But Rybar’s activities extend well beyond Ukraine, with the channel promoting pro-Kremlin narratives in Africa and the Middle East. More recently, it has been accused of amplifying far-right narratives surrounding the migration crisis in Ceuta, a Spanish enclave in north Africa.
“At the moment, the project team is in contact with Russia’s foreign ministry, which is working to resolve the situation. Since there were no violations of local legislation, we expect all detainees to be released,” the channel said on Telegram.
Britain sanctioned Zvinchuk and Rybar in December 2025 over their role in spreading Kremlin propaganda and undermining support for Ukraine. The British government said Zvinchuk received funding from the Russian state-owned defence conglomerate Rostec, and worked with members of Russia’s intelligence services.
The US has separately accused Zvinchuk of attempting to interfere in the 2024 presidential election, offering a reward of up to $10m for information about those involved.
Days before his arrest, Zvinchuk boasted on social media that he had managed to enter Montenegro despite being subject to western sanctions and an entry ban. He mocked a border guard who, he said, had searched his belongings but failed to check his name against a database.
The Kremlin spokesperson, Dmitry Peskov, said Moscow was aware of Zvinchuk’s detention and would work to secure his release.
Russia’s former president Dmitry Medvedev suggested Moscow could detain European and American citizens to use in prisoner exchanges to secure Zvinchuk’s release. “We will probably have to replenish our pool of prisoners for exchange with European and American idiots in order to get our own people back,” he wrote on social media.
The arrest is likely to further strain relations between Montenegro and Russia, which have long been tense. In 2016, Montenegrin authorities accused Russian operatives of plotting with Serbian ultranationalists to stage a coup, allegations Moscow denied.
Montenegro, which joined Nato in 2017 and is seeking membership of the EU, imposed sanctions on Russia after its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
The country recently approved plans to end visa-free travel for Russian citizens from 1 November, closing off a popular holiday destination for Russian tourists as it brings its visa policy into line with the EU.

articles.title: Iran war could force Israel to postpone election, IDF chief tells US officials
articles.body:
IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir has told senior U.S. government and military officials that a renewed military escalation with Iran could force Israel to postpone its general election, currently scheduled for October 27, according to a source familiar with the discussions.
Zamir raised serious concerns about the security and political consequences of another direct confrontation with Tehran, warning that a major outbreak of fighting so close to the vote could make holding the election on schedule impossible. Israel’s security chiefs have already described the weeks leading up to Oct. 27 as a particularly sensitive period and held a joint assessment this week focused on ensuring the election can be held safely.
The warning comes as U.S. President Donald Trump said Thursday that Washington would not attack Iran “at any time prior to the midterm elections” on November 3. Trump said talks with Tehran were “productive,” while insisting that the pressure campaign and blockade against Iran would remain in force.
Despite Trump’s declaration, the IDF remains on heightened alert. The Israeli Air Force and Military Intelligence Directorate are maintaining readiness for a possible escalation with Iran, which the military continues to regard as its primary strategic theater. Any Israeli involvement in another major confrontation with Tehran would be coordinated with Washington.
The IDF and U.S. military have remained in close coordination since the end of the latest round of fighting with Iran. Israeli military intelligence is meanwhile building an extensive new target bank inside Iran, covering ballistic missiles, launch and production infrastructure and sites connected to Tehran’s nuclear program. The IDF declined to comment on Zamir’s reported remarks.
The warning fits a broader pattern of heightened preparations ahead of the election. Zamir recently canceled a planned trip to the United States, where he had been due to meet the commander of U.S. Central Command and the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, saying the security situation made it inappropriate for him to leave Israel.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu also warned during a visit to Tel Nof Air Base last week that there were “signs” Israel’s enemies could attempt an attack ahead of the election. “Don’t mess with us, not now and not ever,” he said. “Our long arm will reach you anywhere and at any time.”

articles.title: Trump envoys, European officials to discuss ‘new ideas’ for Ukraine peace in Miami
articles.body:
Trump envoys, European officials to discuss ‘new ideas’ for Ukraine peace in Miami
US President Donald Trump’s envoys will meet Ukrainian negotiators and European officials in Miami on Friday to discuss a new proposal to end Russia’s war in Ukraine. Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will present ideas developed during recent talks with both sides, one source said Thursday.
President Donald Trump's envoys will meet Ukrainian and European officials in Miami on Friday to discuss "new ideas" and seek a unified proposal to end the war with Russia, two US sources told AFP.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed the talks after a day in which a Russian strike on buses killed 30 people in the frontline city of Kramatorsk, one of the deadliest attacks in weeks.
"The Ukrainian negotiating team is due to meet Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff in the US tomorrow," Zelensky said Thursday. "The meeting is expected to last two days. We are also counting on a European team to join our negotiating group."
Zelensky said his chief of staff, Kyrylo Budanov, as well as Ukraine's top officials: Rustem Umerov, Sergiy Kyslytsya and David Arakhamia will take part in the talks in Florida.
Watch moreBlack sea and black ops: How exposed is Europe to Ukraine war spillover?
The US-led peace efforts to end the Ukraine war have been largely stalled, with Washington focused on its conflict with Iran despite Kyiv saying Russia has ramped up aerial attacks.
But US officials said they were making a fresh effort in an enlarged format, following visits to Moscow and Kyiv by last month by Witkoff, Trump's business friend-turned-roving envoy, and the president's son-in-law Kushner.
"They will discuss new ideas and proposals that American negotiators began developing with the Russians and Ukrainians during their recent visit to the region," one of the US sources familiar with the talks told AFP.
"The American negotiators also invited national security advisors from the United Kingdom, France, and Germany, as well as officials from NATO and the European Union."
US officials said the envoys would discuss "security guarantees for Ukraine, a post-war prosperity plan, and other aspects of the conflict".
They added that the Europeans had expressed "frustrations" to Washington about energy costs – which Trump has blamed on Ukrainian attacks on Russian diesel refineries, rather than his Iran war.
"They are all nervous about the winter. It will be a tough winter if the war does not stop," the US source said.
"So, the United States is trying to mediate with the sides with the goal of creating a unified proposal."
Zelensky said last week that the United States wanted to revive peace efforts by trying to broker a new round of talks with Ukraine and Russia and hold it by the end of October.
The Kremlin said last month that three-way talks on ending the war could take place in October.
Previous rounds of talks have failed to yield tangible progress towards peace, with Moscow unwilling to drop its maximalist conditions to end the fighting.
Trump said earlier this week that he had a call scheduled with Russian President Vladimir Putin, although it was expected to focus on the reported death of a researcher at a Russian plague lab.
In a sign that Ukraine was under discussion, Witkoff was seen by AFP reporters traveling with Trump on Air Force One on Wednesday on a campaign trip to Texas for the US midterm elections.
(FRANCE 24 with AFP)
Keywords for this article

articles.title: NATO asks Russia ‘not to worry’ despite earlier threats
articles.body:
NATO asks Russia ‘not to worry’ despite earlier threats
NATO’s upcoming nuclear drills in Italy are pre-planned and no reason for Russia to “miscalculate,” the bloc’s nuclear policy director, Nassima Barrows, has claimed. The comments came despite NATO’s continued aggressive rhetoric towards Moscow.
On Wednesday, Estonia’s foreign minister claimed to The Times that NATO has the capability to close the Baltic Sea “within hours,” cutting Russia’s economic “lifeline” and creating an “existential” crisis for the country. Last week, Swedish Air Warfare Centre chief Colonel Carl Bergqvist said his country’s warplanes were ready to attack targets deep inside Russian territory in the event of a conflict with Moscow.
NATO said on Thursday that 17 member states will take part in the Steadfast Noon nuclear deterrence exercises between October 13 and 23, further adding to tensions between Russia and the West.
In late September, Moscow sent a stern message to NATO, saying it will use “its entire available arsenal” if the bloc threatens Russia’s Kaliningrad Region. The warning followed major drills by NATO aircraft near the Russian Baltic exclave in August and a later call by Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski for Western nations to increase their military posture near Russian borders so that the authorities in Moscow would be “uncertain of what we will do.”
NATO’s nuclear policy director, Nassima Barrows, told Politico later on Thursday that the fact that the Steadfast Noon drills are held every year should serve as “a clear message to nations like Russia that there is no need to worry.”
“This is predictable and there is no reason to miscalculate,” she added.
The exercises are aimed to “ensure the safety and security of our nuclear capability,” Barrows said.
Politico also cited an unnamed NATO official, who claimed that the bloc’s current intention is “to really keep things calm” with Moscow.
According to the chief of NATO’s nuclear operations, US Colonel David Bull, the drills in Italy will feature “no live nuclear weapons,” with troops expected to train various activities from a “simulated alert to [a] live flight exercise.”
During his speech at a session of the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) in Vienna on Thursday, Russian envoy Dmitry Polyansky reiterated that Moscow “threatens no one and has no intention of attacking anyone.”
At the same time, however, the country “cannot ignore the development of plans by NATO for a direct military clash with Russia, nor the bloc’s simulation of scenarios involving a military-political blockade of Kaliningrad Region,” he stressed.
“Our response to any unfriendly moves will be swift,” Polyansky said, urging NATO against testing Russia’s patience and pushing the European continent “toward the point of no return.”

articles.title: EU supportive of extending UNIFIL Lebanon mandate, says Kallas
articles.body:
Breadcrumb
EU supportive of extending UNIFIL Lebanon mandate, says Kallas
Visiting EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas told AFP on Thursday that the bloc favoured avoiding a security vacuum and extending a UN peacekeeping mandate in south Lebanon, where Israel invaded while fighting Hezbollah.
The EU's top diplomat also said that the bloc would soon be launching a training mission for the Lebanese army, calling it "a major upgrade in the security relationship" with the Mediterranean country.
Lebanon's cash-strapped, under-resourced military faces enormous challenges, including in completing its deployment to south Lebanon under a US-sponsored framework agreement reached between Israel and Lebanon in June.
"Our member states have been saying that there can't be any security vacuum in southern Lebanon, so everybody is worried about the UNIFIL mandate ending," she said in an interview during a visit to Lebanon where she met senior officials.
"It would be most welcomed if this mandate is extended, so that is the position of the member states," she added.
The United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon, which now counts some 7,500 personnel from nearly 50 countries, has been in place since 1978, although its presence has not prevented repeated outbreaks of conflict.
Under US pressure, the UN Security Council voted last year to end UNIFIL's mandate on 31 December 2026.
'Dangerous'
But in March, Lebanese militant group Hezbollah drew the country into the broader Middle East war by attacking Israel, which responded with massive airstrikes and a ground invasion that Lebanon says have killed more than 4,300 people.
Israel now maintains troops in a self-declared "security zone" running around 10 kilometres (six miles) inside Lebanon along the border.
Violence has decreased since a ceasefire following a US-Iran understanding in June, and the US-sponsored Lebanon-Israel framework agreed later that month.
The framework deal involves the disarmament of Hezbollah, a gradual withdrawal of Israeli forces from Lebanon's south and the deployment of the Lebanese army to the region, starting in test areas known as "pilot zones", but the process has largely stalled.
Kallas said that under the deal, "there should be somebody who is verifying whether the parties are keeping to their agreements".
"So, as long as you don't have any kind of international force yet ready to do that... it's dangerous when one mission like UNIFIL ends and the other one has not started yet," she said.
Lebanese officials have repeatedly called for the mandate to be extended.
President Joseph Aoun's office said that he told Kallas that Lebanon is "counting on the support of the European Union to find an alternative formula" for after the UNIFIL mandate ends.
France and Italy, major contributors to UNIFIL, have previously said they are willing to set up a multinational coalition to succeed the force.
EU training mission
Kallas also said a planned EU training and advisory mission would soon be established, emphasising that it would not replace the peacekeepers.
On Monday, "we sit down with the EU foreign ministers to give this final push... to launch this mission", she said.
She expressed hope that the civilian-military mission, which will not only focus on south Lebanon, "would be ready already by the end of this year".
"The focus is on supporting the Lebanese Armed Forces, and supporting the Lebanese Internal Security Forces, in order to keep control of the country and security," she said.
"That means training, that means also working on the capabilities," she added.
"Lebanese sovereignty and territorial integrity is very important. So, it has to be the Lebanese government that is providing services and keeping control of the country," she added.
At a joint press conference with Lebanese Foreign Minister Youssef Raggi, Kallas emphasised that "Lebanon must have full control of its whole territory. That also means moving towards disarmament of Hezbollah".
The EU is a major source of assistance to Lebanon with Kallas noting that in September, the bloc announced 505 million euros ($615 million) in financial assistance until 2027, completing a one billion euro package announced in 2024.
Lebanon is also the third-largest beneficiary of its European Peace Facility fund, she added.
(AFP)

articles.title: Trump reports productive Iran talks and rules out U.S. strikes before midterm elections
articles.body:
U.S. President Donald Trump said Thursday that Washington was holding “productive talks” with Iran and would not launch attacks against the country before the November 3 midterm elections.
Writing on his Truth Social platform, Trump said he “will make it clear to everyone” that the United States would not attack Iran “at any time before the midterm elections, which are held in the US on 3 November.”
He ended the post by stating that “Iran is not going to get a nuclear weapon.”
His comments came amid disagreements over Iran’s nuclear program and efforts to end the seven-month conflict involving the United States, Israel and Iran.
Earlier Thursday, Mohammad Eslami, head of Iran’s atomic energy organization, said Tehran would neither abandon uranium enrichment nor surrender its uranium, according to Iranian state media cited by Reuters.
The statement followed comments Wednesday from U.S. Vice President JD Vance, who told Reuters that Iran must make a “significant” reduction in its uranium enrichment capacity for the war to end.
The United States and Israel launched extensive airstrikes against Iran on February 28.
Iran’s supreme leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, and several senior military officials were killed during the opening days of the conflict.
Iran responded by closing the Strait of Hormuz, a major shipping route that normally carries about one-fifth of the world’s oil.
Since then, negotiations, a memorandum of understanding and ceasefire arrangements have failed to produce a lasting end to the fighting.
A fragile ceasefire is currently in place. U.S. forces have not attacked Iran since September 1, although vessels in the Strait of Hormuz have periodically been struck.

articles.title: Ukrainian forces strike facilities involved in missile launches and production of fuel for Kh-101 missiles
articles.body:
Ukrainian forces strike facilities involved in missile launches and production of fuel for Kh-101 missiles
Ukrainian forces struck Russian facilities involved in missile launches and the production of rocket fuel on the night of 8-9 October.
Source: General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine on Telegram
Quote: "A facility belonging to the Barmin Research Institute of Launch Systems, a branch of the Centre for the Operation of Ground-Based Space Infrastructure Facilities, was struck near the settlement of Dalneye Konstantinovo-5 in Nizhny Novgorod Oblast."
Details: The General Staff noted that the сentre is involved in the development, maintenance and operation of launch facilities, fuelling equipment and control systems for missiles.
The defence forces also struck the Redkino Experimental Plant near the settlement of Redkino in Tver Oblast. The plant is involved in the Russian military-industrial complex's production chains. It manufactures components of Decilin-M fuel for Kh-55 and Kh-101 cruise missiles, as well as additives for diesel fuel and aviation gas. The plant is subject to international sanctions.
"In addition, to weaken the enemy's military-industrial complex's capacity to produce explosives and rocket fuel, the Centre for the Disposal of Intercontinental Ballistic Missiles was struck near the settlement of Surovatikha in Russia's Nizhny Novgorod Oblast," the General Staff added.
It stressed that strikes on such facilities constitute Ukraine's exercise of its inherent right to self-defence under Article 51 of the UN Charter and are aimed at reducing the military, economic and technological potential of the aggressor state.
Background: The General Staff previously reported that the defence forces struck the Omsk Oil Refinery, located more than 2,500 km from Ukraine's state border, on the afternoon of 8 October. This was the second attack on the facility since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

articles.title: Meet the German spymaster turned treason suspect
articles.body:
Europe's biggest spy scandal since the Cold War centers on an octogenarian German suspect
The former head of Germany’s foreign intelligence service built a lucrative second career trading on his security expertise. Now prosecutors accuse him of profiting from secrets belonging to the state.
August Hanning spent seven years at the top of Germany’s foreign intelligence service, the BND, with access to some of the country’s most closely guarded secrets. Then came a second act: private consulting, corporate intelligence and business stretching across Europe, into Russia and Asia.
Now, the 80-year-old former spymaster is himself at the center of an espionage investigation, after German federal prosecutors arrested him Tuesday on suspicion of treasonous espionage, attempted treason and other espionage offenses. They allege he obtained a stream of secret intelligence from his former chief of staff and used the material to benefit his private consulting business.
“It’s catastrophic for Germany and for Western intelligence services. Everyone is in shock. The scale of it is enormous, especially at a moment like this,” said one EU intelligence official, who — like others in this report — was granted anonymity to discuss a clandestine arena. “And given that investigators stumbled across this while working on an entirely separate case, we’re likely to learn much more.”
Advertisement
For the BND, the case comes at an uncomfortable moment. Just last week, German parliamentarians began debating a new law proposed by Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s government to grant the agency sweeping new authority, as part of an effort to return Berlin’s foreign intelligence service to the top ranks of global espionage. The timing is equally awkward for European intelligence more broadly. With Russian hybrid attacks continuously targeting Europe, governments across the bloc are rewriting decades-old security laws to give their spy agencies greater powers and be taken more seriously.
Prosecutors say Hanning’s former chief of staff, identified under German privacy rules as Manfred D., supplied him with roughly 2,000 BND documents between 2010 and June 2022. Many contained classified information intended exclusively for internal intelligence work, including material used to brief senior German officials.
Former BND (Federal Intelligence Service) President August Hanning arrives for the Bundestag hearing on December 4, 2008 in Berlin, Germany. | Carsten Koall/Getty Images
In comments to German newspaper WELT, a lawyer representing Hanning said some of the allegations against the ex-spymaster were true but that he did not harm Germany.
“He was in possession of confidential documents. Incorrect, however, is the accusation that he had passed on information contained therein to the detriment of the Federal Republic of Germany — let alone [for] payment. Further investigations will show that,” he said.
In one case, prosecutors suspect Hanning used classified material to prepare an analysis for an employee of foreign intelligence service. They also allege he maintained a relationship with a representative of another foreign intelligence service for several years, passing along political information that was partly based on material obtained from Manfred D.
Prosecutors have not publicly identified either foreign service but German media has named Azerbaijan and Kazakhstan. Azerbaijan has denied any connection.
Advertisement
“In intelligence services, everything is logged — who accesses which documents and when. If an analyst working on right-wing extremism suddenly started looking at intelligence on China, that would raise red flags. But the position of chief of staff has access to virtually everything, so it wouldn’t look suspicious because of the seniority of the position,” said a second EU intelligence official.
Chiefs of staff often stay on when directors change, unless they don’t get along with the incoming boss, the official added.
“Every intelligence service will now be looking at what information it shared with the BND and assessing what damage may have been done,” he said.
Revolving door
Hanning led the BND from 1998 to 2005, before serving as state secretary at Germany’s interior ministry until 2009. Once out of government, he wasted little time entering the private sector.
In July 2010, Hanning and his wife established Hanning Consult. It was in the spring of that same year that Manfred D. agreed to provide him with intelligence from inside the BND in exchange for payment, according to the prosecutor’s statement. Hanning then used that information in his private consulting activities, they added.
Roderich Kiesewetter, a Christian Democrat lawmaker on the Foreign Affairs Committee in the German parliament, said that within Germany there is a “very widespread network” of people who use the contacts and knowledge acquired while they were in service to influence Berlin’s policy on behalf of foreign governments like Russia and China.
Advertisement
“It’s not only sad, it’s damaging the reputation of Germany,” Kiesewetter told POLITICO. “You could also say if you want to talk to Russia, take former members of the government or former members of the secret services.”
Hanning also became involved with Samuel Danilowitsch, a German businessman, who led the Swiss corporate intelligence consultancy, Pluteos. There, Hanning eventually became chairman and the two were listed as attending a 2019 Moscow gathering focused on Europe-Russia relations, attended by Russian political and business figures, where the annexation of Crimea was brought up as a “necessity” rather than a choice. Pluteos did not respond to a request for comment.
From around 2014, Hanning joined British consultancy G3 as a senior adviser, according to archived web pages seen by POLITICO. He later oversaw its work involving Russia and the former Soviet republics, according to German media outlet Correctiv. G3 did not respond to a request for comment.
In 2019, Hanning was invited as a “guest of honor” to a gathering organized by Russia’s Security Council of officials and experts from Arctic Council countries. It was chaired by former secretary of the Security Council of Russia, Nikolai Patrushev, one of the most powerful figures in President Vladimir Putin’s security orbit. As part of the cultural program, the group visited the remote Valaam Island monastery where Hanning was pictured next to Patrushev.
Delegates from Arctic Council countries visited the Valaam Island monastery. August Hanning stands on the far right of the front row, next to senior Russian security official Nikolai Patrushev. | Valaam monastery
Hanning has also publicly ventured into some of the more politically explosive questions surrounding Russia’s war on Ukraine.
In 2024, he told WELT TV that he considered it “very likely” that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy knew about the 2022 operation that destroyed the Nord Stream pipelines. Days later, Hanning went further, suggesting an agreement between senior Ukrainian and Polish figures was behind the attack. Germany has since charged a Ukrainian national it identified only as Serhii K., with his trial due to begin in Hamburg in October.
Advertisement
None of those business relationships, contacts or statements establishes a connection to the espionage case now facing Hanning, though they paint a picture of the influence he continued to amass after leaving the German government. Prosecutors have not accused him of spying for Russia.
The steakhouse heiress
Investigators got onto Hanning’s trail starting with an extraordinary custody dispute involving Christina Block, an heiress to a German steakhouse empire.
Block is accused by the Hamburg Public Prosecutor’s Office of orchestrating the abduction of her two youngest children from their father in Denmark. Prosecutors in that case say Block and two men commissioned an Israeli security team to seize her children, then aged 10 and 13, from their father, Stephan Hensel.
According to the indictment, masked men beat Hensel and took the children across the Danish-German border, to southern Germany. The children were reunited with their father in Denmark four days later, under a court order. Block denies knowing about the abduction.
In September 2025, Hamburg investigators searched Hanning’s home and business premises in connection with the Block case, according to local media. Prosecutors suspected Hanning and a retired police officer had accepted a contract worth more than €100,000 to intercept the children on their way to school in November 2022. The plan ultimately failed as their father noticed suspicious figures and alerted Danish police.
German broadcaster Taggeschau reported that the investigators, in the search of Hanning’s premises, discovered around 2,000 digital BND documents that ultimately triggered scrutiny of his handling of sensitive government information. Federal prosecutors took over the resulting investigation in May 2026.
Advertisement
Manfred D. had been Hanning’s chief of staff at the intelligence service and subsequently served several of Hanning’s successors, remaining in a senior position until March this year.
Both men are now in custody.
“He’s reflecting the Germany between 1998 and 2011, so he has not the feeling of having done something evil,” said Kiesewetter. “He was just mirroring [the] state policy of the center-right Christian Democratic and conservative political alliance.”

articles.title: AFU General Staff: Facilities involved in missile launches, rocket fuel production inside Russia struck last night
articles.body:
The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) reported strikes carried out last night against enemy facilities involved in missile launches and rocket fuel production, specifically in Nizhny Novgorod and Tver regions.
"On the night of October 9, 2026, units of the Ukrainian Defense Forces struck facilities within the Russian Federation. Specifically, a facility belonging to a branch of JSC Center for Operation of Ground-Based Space Infrastructure Facilities—the V.P. Barmin Research Institute of Launch Complexes—was hit near the settlement of Dalneye Konstantinovo-5 in Nizhny Novgorod region," the General Staff stated on Telegram on Friday.
It is noted that the Centre operates in the sphere of creating, maintaining, and operating launch complexes, fueling equipment, and control systems for missiles.
Furthermore, the Redkino Experimental Plant, which is part of the enemy's military-industrial complex supply chains, was struck near the settlement of Redkino in Tver region. The plant produces Decilin-M fuel components for Kh-55 and Kh-101 cruise missiles, as well as additives for diesel fuel and aviation kerosene. It is subject to international sanctions.
Additionally, in an effort to weaken the Russian military-industrial complex' capacity to produce explosives and rocket fuel, a strike was carried out against the Intercontinental Ballistic Missile Decommissioning Center (near the settlement of Surovatikha, Nizhny Novgorod region, Russia).

articles.title: Pentagon prepares 3-day intensive Iran strike option as Trump says no attack before midterms: NYT
articles.body:
Seyit Kurt
09 October 2026•Update: 09 October 2026
The Pentagon has drawn up plans for an intensive three-day military campaign against Iran, the New York Times reported on Thursday, even as President Donald Trump said Washington will not launch an attack before the Nov. 3 midterm elections.
The US military, acting on Trump's orders, has developed options to strike Iran's missile and drone arsenal, energy facilities and other military sites, The Times reported, citing US officials.
Senior national security officials, led by Vice President JD Vance, discussed the plans at Camp David last Friday, with the options centering on a short, intensive campaign lasting about three days, according to people briefed on the proposal.
The strikes would focus on Iran's missile and drone arsenal, much of which has been rebuilt by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) since the early phase of the war, the newspaper said.
Other potential targets include Iranian energy facilities as well as IRGC command posts and headquarters.
Axios separately reported that the Pentagon ordered the US Central Command (CENTCOM) several days ago to complete preparations for a possible resumption of major combat operations against Iran.
The directive did not set a date for strikes and Trump had not made a final decision, Axios said, adding that any renewed major combat operations were expected to include large-scale bombing of Iranian energy, infrastructure and nuclear targets.
The military preparations come as Trump said on Thursday that the US would not attack Iran before the Nov. 3 midterm elections, while pointing to ongoing diplomatic efforts.
In a post on his Truth Social platform, Trump said Washington and Tehran were having "productive discussions."
The NYT also reported that Trump has repeatedly declined proposals in recent months to resume major combat operations against Iran, despite ordering the Pentagon to prepare new options.
Three US aircraft carriers are expected to be in the Middle East in the coming weeks as part of the major military buildup, according to the newspaper.

articles.title: Ukraine war latest: Russian glide bomb strikes in Kramatorsk kill at least 33
articles.body:
Key developments on Oct. 8:
- At least 33 dead after Russian glide bomb strikes Kramatorsk buses
- Russian drone barrage on Kyiv kills 4, injures 19, disrupts electricity, water supplies
- Polish SIM cards found in Russian drones downed in Poland
- US, Russia confirm Trump's latest Ukraine peace push is falling apart
- Ukraine strikes Russia's Omsk oil refinery in Siberia, General Staff confirms
- UK ramps up sanctions against Russian shadow fleet, crypto industry, big oil
A Russian glide bomb strike on two minibuses in Kramatorsk killed 33 people on the morning of Oct. 8, Ukraine's emergency service (DSNS) said.
Twenty-two more people were injured in the Russian attack, Donetsk regional governor Vadym Filashkin said. Fire broke out in at least two busses following the Russian strikes, according to DSNS.
"Russia comes to the Ukrainian land with death. She hits our cities, kills our people and multiplies her crimes every day," Filashkin said.
President Volodymyr Zelensky said that doctors were still fighting for the lives of some of the injured people and warned that the number of dead may still increase. Two dead people could not yet be identified due to the severity of their injuries, he added.
"This strike will not go without our response. Russia is trying to destroy all life in Donbas, and the world needs to react to this," Zelensky said.
The Kramatorsk and Sloviansk military administrations ordered the stop of all public transport.
"The Russians are targeting civilians. For them, a bus with passengers is an attractive target precisely because one hit can kill as many people as possible," Filashkin said.
Across Ukraine's Donetsk Oblast, four more people had been killed and six injured by Russian attacks as of the morning of Oct. 8, prior to the Kramatorsk strike, according to the governor.
In total, Russian forces shelled settlements in the Donetsk region 31 times over the last day, and 256 people, including 32 children, were evacuated from the front line, according to the Donetsk governor.
read also
Russian drone barrage on Kyiv kills 4, injures 19, disrupts electricity, water supplies
Russian drone strikes on Oct. 8 have killed four people and injured at least 19 in Kyiv, the city's authorities said.
A Russian drone struck a four-story commercial building in Solomyanskyi district, killing two and injuring two, and leading to a fire, while the wreckage of another fell on the Holosiivskyi district, Klitschko said.
Prior to that strike, Klitschko said that Russian attacks on the capital this morning had killed one person and injured 11 others.
A fourth person died of their injuries in hospital, the Kyiv city military administration (KMDA) said in the afternoon.
Klitschko raised the number of injured to 19, 13 of which were hospitalized, in an update on 07:21 p.m. local time.
At 10:00 a.m. local time, Ukraine’s biggest private energy firm DTEK announced emergency energy shutdowns in Brovary, Buchanskyi, Vyshgorod, and Boryspil districts of the oblast.
Shortly after, KMDA announced that the right bank of Kyiv may experience interruptions in water supply, as the power decrease in the electricity grid also meant a decrease in pressure of the water supply network. This applied especially to the Holosiivskyi, Sviatoshynskyi, Solomyanskyi and Shevchenkivskyi districts.
The drop in voltage from external power supply centers also temporarily halted Kyiv Metro train services and escalator operations, the KMDA said.
DSNS also said that a fire broke out at a logistics facility in the Buchanskyi district in Kyiv Oblast following a Russian drone strike.
In Sviatopetrivske in Buchanskyi district, a school-kindergarten and a nearby playground in a residential complex were damaged in the attack, Kyiv Oblast Governor Tymur Tkachenko said. In another settlement in the district, a woman was injured and hospitalized, he added.
Overnight, Russian drone strikes on Kyiv had already killed four people and injured 21 across four districts, KMDA said.
read also
Polish SIM cards found in Russian drones downed in Poland
Polish military prosecutors found Polish SIM cards in some of the Russian drones downed during a Russian mass drone incursion into the country on the night of Sept. 9 to Sept. 10, 2025, RMF24 reported on Oct. 8.
Polish authorities didn't disclose whether three Polish SIM cards had been stolen or obtained illegaly, according to RMF24. The investigation was discontinued after it did not lead to the identification of the specific people responsible for the Russian incursion.
"The investigation was discontinued because the perpetrator of the crime of violating Polish airspace and thus posing a threat to public safety was not identified," Marcin Kozak, spokesman of the District Prosecutor’s Office in Lublin, said.
On Sept. 9, 2025, more than 30 Gerbera-type drones breached Polish airspace, some of which were shot down by the Polish military, RMF24 reported.
read also
US, Russia confirm Trump's latest Ukraine peace push is falling apart
Ending Russia's war against Ukraine through negotiations is currently unattainable, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio told Greek media outlet Kathimerini on Oct. 8, casting further doubt on President Donald Trump's latest push to broker peace.
The comments confirm earlier Kyiv Independent reporting that Washington's latest effort to advance negotiations faces growing uncertainty.
At this point, there appears to be no prospect of a negotiated settlement, Rubio said. He added that the goal remains out of reach because Russia insists on gaining full control over Ukraine's Donetsk Oblast without fighting, a demand Kyiv has rejected.
The latest rounds of peace negotiations have also stalled over Moscow's territorial demands.
The Kremlin has repeatedly rejected a ceasefire and demanded that Kyiv surrender the partially occupied Donbas, a strategically important region in eastern Ukraine. Moscow is effectively seeking territory that Russian forces have failed to capture militarily.
Ukraine has instead called for a ceasefire along the current front line.
The diplomatic effort now faces another obstacle: Moscow has given little indication that it intends to take part in further talks. Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergey Ryabkov said on Oct. 7 that there were currently no plans for U.S.-mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine.
"There are currently no plans to hold talks in this format," Ryabkov told reporters.
The latest effort began in early September, when Trump's envoys traveled to Kyiv and Moscow seeking progress before the U.S. midterm elections. The trips produced one tangible outcome: an agreement in principle to hold a trilateral meeting between Ukraine, Russia, and the U.S.
A month later, however, even the trilateral meeting remains uncertain.
President Volodymyr Zelensky said Oct. 8 that Ukrainian negotiators will meet with Trump's envoys in the U.S. later this week to discuss the prospects for peace talks with Russia.
read also
Ukraine strikes Russia's Omsk oil refinery in Siberia, General Staff confirms
Ukraine's General Staff confirmed that its forces struck Russia's Omsk oil refinery in Russia's Omsk Oblast on Oct. 8.
"The destruction of such facilities is the exercise by Ukraine of its inalienable right to self-defense in accordance with Article 51 of the UN Charter and is aimed at reducing the military-economic potential of the Russian Federation," the General Staff said.
Ukrainian drone manufacturer Fire Point had previously reported an attack on the refinery, saying that the refinery was hit with its own long-range FP-1 attack drones.
Videos and images from local residents, shared by Ukrainian monitoring channels, show explosions, fire, and smoke rising from the area surrounding the oil refinery.
Omsk Oblast Governor Vitaly Khotsenko confirmed that there was a drone attack on the region. Ukrainian authorities have not yet confirm a strike on the refinery.
Omsk is located in southwestern Siberia, north of the Kazakh border. The city of more than 1 million people is some 2,500 kilometers (about 1,550 miles) east of Ukraine controlled territory.
The Omsk oil refinery is owned by Russia's state-owned energy giant Gazprom. It's the country's largest refinery by refining capacity, processing more than 21 million metric tons of crude oil per year.
The plant produces a wide range of fuels, lubricants, and petrochemical products and is involved in supplying the Russian military, Ukraine's General Staff said after Ukraine struck the refinery on July 6. According to the military, the facility has a refining depth of about 99%, one of the highest rates in Russia.
Earlier, an overnight Ukrainian strike on the Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat oil refinery in Russia's Bashkortostan region caused a large blaze at the plant, Ukraine's General Staff confirmed on Oct. 8.
read also
UK ramps up sanctions against Russian shadow fleet, crypto industry, big oil
The U.K. published 38 new sanctions listings on Oct. 8, targeting ships helping Russia evade existing sanctions and a range of companies in Moscow's military-industrial complex, energy, and cryptocurrency sectors.
"The message is simple: if you help Russia fund or equip this war, you will face the consequences," reads a U.K. government press release.
Among the businesses in the new sanctions listings are three cryptocurrency exchanges and two payment platforms.
Xeltox Enterprises, one of those listed entities has "been involved in obtaining a benefit from or supporting the government of Russia by carrying on business in a sector of strategic significance (...) the financial services sector," reads the U.K. government's sanctions listing.
Russia has increasingly sought to use cryptocurrency, which is hard to track, to circumvent global sanctions, and the new U.K. sanctions target the "A7" network, which is at the heart of Moscow's attempts to evade financial sanctions.
That has prompted the U.K., the U.S., the EU, and Ukraine to target crypto schemes in recent sanctions packages.
Also featuring on the listings are two further oil companies: Zarubezhneft and INK Capital.
"The U.K. was the first country in the G7 to sanction the top four Russian oil companies," reads the press statement.
The U.K. has also added 12 ships to its list of sanctioned vessels accused of being part of Russia's shadow fleet — dilapidated vessels suspected of helping Moscow evade price caps and bans on its trade in oil and gas.
That takes the number of ships sanctioned by the U.K. to 645 and the total number of Russia sanctions to 3,537.

articles.title: Two 14-year-old boys killed by an explosive device in a field in Sumy Oblast
articles.body:
Two 14-year-old boys were killed when an explosive device detonated in the evening in the Konotop district of Sumy Oblast, according to the statement by Oleh Hryhorov, head of the Sumy Regional Military Administration. The children encountered the dangerous device in a field, suffered severe injuries, and died at the scene, the statement said.
In 2022, Russian forces occupied parts of Sumy Oblast, but Ukraine liberated the region in April. Russia intensified its offensive again in 2025. Today, mines, unexploded ordnance and Russian drones shot down over the region pose a danger, as their warheads can detonate after falling. Overall, 146 children in Ukraine have suffered mine-related injuries, former Interior Minister Ihor Klymenko reported in April. For example, two months ago, an 11-year-old boy and a 15-year-old boy in Sumy Oblast were injured when an explosive device detonated.
Hryhorov expressed his condolences to the parents and relatives of the victims and urged people to remain cautious:
“Please be as careful as possible and remind children: do not approach unknown or suspicious objects, touch them, or try to move them. Take care of yourselves and your loved ones,” Hryhorov said.
Demining efforts continue in Sumy Oblast
On 24 February 2022, Russian forces entered the territory of Sumy Oblast. The first battles in the region took place that same day. In particular, Russian forces attempted to break through to Sumy, but Ukrainian troops repelled the offensive. On 11 April 2022, Ukraine restored control over the entire Sumy region.
As early as 7 June 2022, deminers were working in the Konotop, Sumy, and Okhtyrka districts, according to the Government Portal. That day, they surveyed areas and neutralized explosive devices.
The work of deminers remains deadly dangerous. In September 2024, two pyrotechnicians from Dnipropetrovsk Oblast were hit by a mine while demining Sumy Oblast: one died, while the other was hospitalized. In July 2025, deminer Oleh Petrenko was killed during humanitarian demining operations in Shostka District when a Russian FPV drone detonated, the State Emergency Service of Ukraine reported. Another pyrotechnician was injured, the statement said.
Nevertheless, the work continues despite the danger. In 2025, State Emergency Service deminers in the Sumy Oblast found and neutralized 5,283 explosive devices, the agency said in April. Sumy Oblast ranked sixth among all Ukrainian regions by this figure.
Twenty-two percent of Ukraine’s territory is potentially contaminated with explosive devices — more than 133,000 square kilometers, former Interior Minister Ihor Klymenko reported in April this year. Since the beginning of the full-scale invasion, State Emergency Service and National Police deminers have surveyed more than 248,000 hectares of territory and found more than 1 million 112 thousand explosive devices, the statement said.

articles.title: Trump envoys pitching ‘new ideas’ to settle Ukraine conflict – media
articles.body:
Trump envoys pitching ‘new ideas’ to settle Ukraine conflict – media
US President Donald Trump’s top negotiators are preparing to pitch “new ideas and proposals” aimed at breaking the deadlock in the Ukraine conflict, with talks involving representatives of Kiev and its European backers scheduled to begin in Miami on Friday, according to Reuters and Axios.
US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner are expected to hold a two-day working session with the Ukrainian delegation in an effort to develop a unified proposal that could later be presented to the Kremlin.
The pair could then travel to Moscow later this month for another round of talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin, Axios reported, citing a source familiar with the discussions.
According to Reuters, the ideas were developed during and after Witkoff and Kushner’s diplomatic tour of Moscow and Kiev in early September. The pair have since remained in contact with both Russian and Ukrainian officials while working on an updated peace initiative.
One proposal reportedly under consideration is a partial ceasefire covering attacks on energy infrastructure and Black Sea shipping. The talks are also expected to address possible security guarantees for Ukraine, a post-conflict economic plan and other elements of a potential settlement.
Witkoff and Kushner met Trump on Thursday to present the latest proposals and receive his input ahead of the Miami talks, according to Axios. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Deputy National Security Adviser Mike Needham also attended the meeting.
Kiev's European backers ‘nervous’ about winter
Kiev will reportedly be represented by Vladimir Zelensky’s chief of staff, Kirill Budanov, intelligence chief Rustem Umerov, diplomatic adviser Sergey Kislitsa and top lawmaker David Arakhamia.
National security advisers from Britain, France and Germany, as well as representatives of NATO and the EU, have also reportedly been invited.
A US source told AFP that European governments have privately complained about soaring energy prices and other economic costs stemming from the conflict, adding that there is growing concern about another winter of hostilities.
“They are all nervous about the winter. It will be a tough winter if the war does not stop,” the source said.
Trump has also repeatedly pressed Zelensky to stop “hurting the world” and halt Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries, arguing that the attacks are worsening a global diesel shortage and driving up fuel costs in the US.
Kremlin agrees with Rubio on ‘stalemate’
The new diplomatic push comes as US Secretary of State Marco Rubio described the conflict as a “dangerous stalemate,” warning that further escalation could spill beyond Ukraine and trigger a broader confrontation.
“This war needs to end in a negotiated settlement. The sooner, the better,” Rubio told reporters in Lisbon on Thursday, while cautioning that Washington would not invest indefinitely in “pointless processes” that produce no progress.
The Kremlin said it shared Rubio’s assessment of the current diplomatic impasse, with spokesman Dmitry Peskov saying he “agreed” that no clear prospect of a negotiated settlement was currently visible.
He nevertheless reiterated Moscow’s position that Russia remains open to negotiations, while accusing Kiev of showing no willingness to accept reality and pursue a long-term settlement.
Despite the lack of progress on Ukraine, contacts between Washington and Moscow have continued on other tracks, Peskov added, noting that the two countries are discussing “a whole range” of potentially mutually beneficial economic projects, including possible cooperation in the energy sector.

articles.title: Ukraine preparing response to new wave of Russian escalation – Zelensky

articles.title: Russian Strikes Near Poland Trigger Military Aviation Deployment and Air Defense Alert
articles.body:
- Category

Russian Strikes Near Poland Trigger Military Aviation Deployment and Air Defense Alert
Poland activated military aviation and placed air defense and radar systems on alert on October 9 as Russia struck targets in western Ukraine.
Poland’s Operational Command of the Armed Forces announced the measures on the same day in a post on X, noting that military aircraft were operating in Polish airspace.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
"Ground-based air defense systems and radar reconnaissance assets have reached a state of readiness," the command stated.
The measures were described as preventive and intended to secure Polish airspace, particularly in areas bordering parts of Ukraine affected by the Russian strikes. The command added that its forces remained ready to respond while monitoring the situation.
Poland has repeatedly taken similar precautionary measures during Russian aerial attacks on western Ukraine, deploying military aircraft and increasing the readiness of air defense and radar systems near the Ukrainian border.
Earlier, on September 21, Poland scrambled military aviation and brought its ground-based air defenses to readiness during Russian strikes on Ukraine, standing down later that night with no airspace violation recorded.
Polish fighter jets had also taken off overnight on September 15 as Russia struck western Ukraine with jet-powered drones. Two days later, Russian drone strikes in Ukraine's Volyn region, where one drone came down roughly four kilometers from the Polish border, prompted Poland to deploy aircraft and briefly suspend operations at the Lublin and Rzeszów airports.

articles.title: Australia asks U.S. for $300M Tomahawk planning system
articles.body:
- The U.S. State Department approved a possible $300 million sale of Tomahawk mission planning systems and support to Australia.
- Australia first fired a Tomahawk from HMAS Brisbane in December 2024 and plans to field the missile on destroyers, frigates and future submarines.
The U.S. State Department has approved a possible $300 million sale to Australia of the systems and support it needs to plan Tomahawk cruise missile strikes, adding mission-planning capability to the long-range missiles the Royal Australian Navy began acquiring in 2023.
The package covers a Theater Mission Planning Center with its associated communications systems, the Tomahawk Mission Planning System, and program management, engineering, training and logistics support for developing and delivering the planning system, according to the Oct. 8 notification to Congress. The approval does not mean the sale is final; the quantities, contract terms and timeline will be set if Australia moves ahead.
A Tomahawk does not simply fly in a straight line to its target. Before launch, planners build a route for the missile, with waypoints over land and sea, terrain and navigation data, and the aim point it is meant to hit. The Theater Mission Planning Center is the system the United States uses to prepare and distribute that data to launching ships and submarines, and the State Department said the sale would strengthen Australia’s Tomahawk capability and deepen its interoperability with U.S. maritime forces.
The principal contractors would be BAE Systems in San Diego, California; Tapestry Solutions, a Boeing subsidiary in St. Louis, Missouri; Peraton in San Jose, California; and Leidos in Virginia Beach, Virginia. The State Department said the sale would not require sending additional U.S. government or contractor personnel to Australia and would not affect U.S. readiness.
Australia announced in 2023 that it would buy Tomahawks for its Hobart-class destroyers and later its Hunter-class frigates, with more than 200 missiles planned. The missiles are also intended for the Virginia-class nuclear-powered attack submarines Australia is set to receive under the AUKUS agreement in the early 2030s. Canberra says the Tomahawk has a range of up to 2,500 km (about 1,550 miles), making it the longest-reaching strike weapon in the Australian Defence Force.
In December 2024, the destroyer HMAS Brisbane fired a Tomahawk for the first time during a test off San Diego, making Australia the third country, after the United States and the United Kingdom, to acquire and fire the missile. That firing followed Australian Navy tests earlier that year of the Naval Strike Missile and Standard Missile-6 from another Hobart-class destroyer, HMAS Sydney.

articles.title: Ukraine to Get Tens of Thousands of SPYS Interceptor Drones Built to Hunt Russia’s Jet Shaheds
articles.body:
- Category
- Defense Tech
Ukraine to Get Tens of Thousands of SPYS Interceptor Drones Built to Hunt Russia’s Jet Shaheds
German defense company Quantum Systems plans to supply Ukraine with tens of thousands of SPYS interceptor drones designed, among other missions, to counter Russia’s new jet-powered Geran-4 and Geran-5 UAVs, company Vice President Matthias Lehna said during a press briefing in Berlin, according to Ukrinform on October 7.
“Over the weekend, an LOI [letter of intent] was signed to provide a package of tens of thousands of SPYS, which, as already mentioned, are capable of shooting down jet-powered drones,” Lehna said.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
SPYS was developed jointly by Quantum Systems and Ukrainian partner WIY through their joint venture, Quantum WIY Industries.
According to the company, experience gained from operating earlier systems in Ukraine—including the STRILA interceptor drone—was incorporated directly into the development of the new platform.
Quantum Systems also said Ukraine has become significantly more effective at countering Russia’s jet-powered UAVs, which are faster and more difficult to intercept than conventional propeller-driven Shahed-type drones.
“Initially, we observed an interception capability in Ukraine at a very low percentage. Then it increased to more than 30%, and recent nights have shown an increase to more than 50%,” a company representative said.
The company stressed, however, that the improvement cannot be attributed to interceptor drones alone. Ukraine has built a layered response that combines multiple air defense systems, fighter aircraft, and increasingly specialized anti-drone platforms.
“But this is a combination of different measures. Ukraine has also adapted, deployed different capabilities, makes extensive use of its F-16 fleet, which is capable of intercepting jet-powered Shaheds. And it is increasingly using developments from companies like ours, which, within this mix of capabilities for countering the new threat, are demonstrating increasingly greater effectiveness,” the Quantum Systems representative said.
The planned SPYS package could become one of the largest interceptor-drone deliveries announced for Ukraine so far. Quantum Systems said it can build on manufacturing infrastructure already established for the STRILA interceptor, allowing production to scale quickly.
“And I’m talking here about several thousand per month,” Lehna said when discussing potential output.
Asked when Ukraine could begin receiving SPYS drones under the new package, he said deliveries could start almost immediately.
“Thousands of units are ready for delivery this year,” Lehna said.
Previously, reports emerged that Russia is increasingly using jet-powered drones in attacks against Ukraine.
Such systems now account for approximately 40% of all UAVs deployed in strikes, with their share potentially rising to around 80% in the future.
